subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the young woman in <Picture 1>, and the whisky bottle she holds upright in her left hand is part of her fixed appearance rather than a separate object. She has long wavy dark-brown hair with wispy centre-parted bangs, small gold hoop earrings, and a slim beaded silver bracelet on her right wrist, and wears a white lace off-shoulder cropped top with ruffled lace along the neckline, the sleeves and the hem, a long white ribbon bow hanging from the centre front down over her bare midriff, and a mustard-yellow and brown plaid pleated skirt with a white waistband and two dark round buttons at the centre front. Her left arm stays bent with the forearm raised, holding the bottle upright at chest-to-shoulder height on her left side, gripped by the neck with four fingers around the right of the neck and the thumb pressing the left, so the cork remains fully visible above her fingers. The bottle is a very tall and slender clear glass whisky bottle, about 3.5 times as tall as its widest body width, with straight sides, a thick flat base, gently rounded shoulders and a short narrow neck; it is closed by a single solid natural cork stopper in pale wood-tone beige-tan, slightly wider than the neck with a softly rounded top edge and a narrow pale glass bead ring beneath it, with no metal capsule, no foil, no screw cap, no wax and no red band anywhere on the closure; faint raised glass lettering is embossed around the shoulder and catches only soft highlights; the glass is filled with deep amber-gold whisky right up to the shoulder, leaving only the short neck empty. A paper label in warm cream-tan, a light caramel-beige and not white, wraps the lower two thirds of the body, printed in dark serif type with a large wordmark at the top, a fine rule beneath it, a second line in serif capitals, a second fine rule, then two short bold serif lines, then several lines of small print, then a tall large numeral at the lower left with tiny text beneath, then a long rule, then a dense block of small print, and at the bottom edge the volume marking on the left and the alcohol strength on the right; on the right side of the label sits a small vertically elongated oval emblem in thin concentric orange-red outlines. Her appearance, hair, costume and the bottle stay fixed for the whole clip; her dance performance, limb positions and timing come from <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> is the night-time indoor setting shown in <Picture 1>: a floor-to-ceiling window behind her with a blurred city skyline and scattered warm bokeh lights at night, a taupe curtain along the left side, and several small potted plants in white ceramic pots on a windowsill at the lower right, lit by warm indoor light from the front.
<Video 1> is the motion and music reference for the target video. It supplies the dance choreography, the body and limb movement, the weight shifts and the second-by-second timing, together with its synchronized audio track; it does not supply identity, costume, props, environment or framing.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized audio track of <Video 1>, an upbeat dance-pop track, and it is reused 1:1 as the complete final audio track of the target video.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] The target video makes <Subject 1>, exactly as she appears in <Picture 1>, re-perform in full the dance from <Video 1> while keeping the bottle gripped in her left hand, inside <Subject 2>, in a single continuous vertical take. Because the source choreography is performed with two free hands, the routine is split: her right hand carries the complete paw-gesture sequence from <Video 1>, while her left arm stays bent and raised, holding the bottle at chest-to-shoulder height and only echoing the vertical bounce, so the bottle stays upright, readable and inside frame throughout. Only motion, timing and music come from <Video 1>; identity, costume, bottle and setting all come from <Picture 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the facial identity, long wavy dark-brown hair with wispy centre-parted bangs, gold hoop earrings, beaded silver bracelet, white lace off-shoulder cropped top with its ruffled edges and long front ribbon bow, and the mustard-yellow plaid pleated skirt with white waistband and dark buttons from <Picture 1> are retained unchanged. The bottle in her left hand also stays unchanged: its 3.5-to-1 slender proportion, straight sides, thick flat base, soft shoulders and short narrow neck, the solid pale wood-tone natural cork stopper with its rounded top and the narrow pale glass bead beneath it, the faint raised lettering around the shoulder, the deep amber-gold whisky filled to the shoulder, and the warm cream-tan label with its large dark wordmark, fine rules, bold serif lines, small numeral block, dense fine print, volume and strength markings and the small orange-red concentric oval emblem all remain exactly as in <Picture 1>; the closure never becomes metal, foil, screw-cap, wax or red, the fill level never rises or falls, the label never turns white and never changes its layout, and the bottle is never released, opened, poured or drunk from.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the night window with its blurred city skyline and warm bokeh, the taupe curtain, the white ceramic potted plants on the windowsill and the warm frontal indoor light are retained.
<Video 1> (dance motion and timing): attribute_transfer - the full-body dance choreography, the arm and hand gesture sequence, the hip sways, head tilts, weight shifts and the second-by-second timing are transferred onto <Subject 1>, while the original performer's identity, costume, environment and audio are not carried over.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track, so the music, its tempo and its exact beat placement match <Video 1> from first frame to last.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic vertical smartphone home-dance clip in a casual, un-staged style, lit warmly from the front, framed as one continuous shot with no cuts, with the same bright indoor key light and soft shadow of <Picture 1>. <Audio 1> plays from the very first frame at an unchanged tempo and every bounce lands on its beat.
[Shot 1] The frame opens with <Subject 1> seen from behind at the centre of <Subject 2>, her long wavy dark-brown hair falling down her back, her right arm bent with a loose fist lifted near shoulder level, and the bottle held at her left side. Within the first half-second she pivots on the spot to face the camera, her hair and the long white ribbon sweeping outward with the turn and a little motion blur trailing across the rotation. She settles into a frontal medium shot framed from head to mid-thigh, the night window and its city lights behind her, the taupe curtain at the left edge, the potted plants at the lower right, and she looks exactly as she does in <Picture 1>.
From about 00:01.000 she runs the source choreography on the beat of <Audio 1>. Her right hand carries the full gesture: the elbow bends and the loose fist rises to beside her right cheek, where it opens and closes four times in time with the beat while her shoulder bounces, exactly as her right hand appears in <Picture 1>. Her left arm stays bent and raised the whole time, holding the bottle upright at chest-to-shoulder height, and drives it through the same small vertical bounce as the beat — a few centimetres at most — so the bottle never dips toward the bottom of frame, never crosses in front of her face, and the cork stays fully visible above her fingers, with the cream-tan label uncovered and facing the camera. The bottle looks exactly as it does in <Picture 1> and never changes: the closure stays a bare pale wood-tone cork with its narrow glass bead beneath, the shoulder keeps its faint raised lettering, the whisky stays filled to the shoulder, the label keeps its warm cream-tan tone and its dark serif wordmark, and the small orange-red concentric oval emblem stays small and sharp. There is only ever one bottle in the frame, still in her hand, never duplicated and never floating.
Through the middle of the take she adds the source video's hip sways and head tilts: her head tips to one side and swings back, her right fist drops to brush her chin and cheek in a small beckoning gesture and returns to its raised position three times, the pleats of her plaid skirt flare and close with each sway, and the long white ribbon swings across her midriff. Her left arm stays steady but relaxed, letting the bottle move only with her torso, so it reads as held rather than carried.
Later the sways widen: her torso leans left and recovers, then leans right and recovers, her hair lifts off her shoulders and swings across her back, and the white ribbon sweeps almost horizontally to the side before falling back. Her right fist pumps upward twice, and her left arm lifts the bottle a little and settles it back to the same height. She keeps her eyes on the lens throughout, alternating a closed-lip smile with an open-mouthed grin as if mouthing along to the music, with no intelligible words. The clip ends with her facing the camera, right fist still raised and the bottle upright at her left side with the label still uncovered and readable, and neither her costume, her hair nor any part of the bottle has changed since the first frame.

overall_soundscape:
The ambience layer copied from <Audio 1> runs through the whole video, carrying the original take's indoor room tone with its light fabric rustle and soft footfalls, with no dialogue and no narration.

non_diegetic_music:
<Audio 1> is directly reused as the complete audience-only score, an upbeat dance-pop track at a steady mid-tempo that drives the rhythm of her fist bounces, hip sways and head tilts, with nothing added, removed, re-timed or replaced.
